nary_nodes.label: Lalique museum jewelry heist
evidence: Burglars stole millions of dollars worth of jewelry from the museum of French luxury glassmaker Lalique in a daring early-morning raid on Sunday

nary_nodes.label: Break-in at Lalique museum
evidence: A gang of masked thieves broke in to the museum in Wingen-sur-Moder in northeastern France around 5:30 am, forcing a door before heading for the jewelry room and smashing open six display cases

nary_nodes.label: Estimated loss from heist
evidence: The loss is currently being assessed but could amount to several million euros, likely close to four million (over $4.5 million)
Around twenty pieces of jewelry were stolen. The loss is currently being assessed but could amount to several million euros, likely close to four million (over $4.5 million)

nary_nodes.label: Number of stolen jewelry pieces
evidence: Around twenty pieces of jewelry were stolen.

nary_nodes.label: Stolen jewelry material
evidence: the stolen jewelry was crystal, without precious gems, and could not be melted down.
Another source close to the investigation said the stolen jewelry was crystal, without precious gems, and could not be melted down.

nary_nodes.label: Museum closure after burglary
evidence: The museum said on its website that it will be closed for several day because of the burglary.

nary_nodes.label: Alarm and delayed response
evidence: An alarm went off, but by the time the security company had completed its checks, it was a cleaning lady who arrived first on the scene and called the police.

nary_nodes.label: Examination of CCTV footage
evidence: The CCTV footage is currently being examined.

nary_nodes.label: Opening of Lalique museum
evidence: The museum, dedicated to the Art Nouveau and Art Deco jeweler and glassmaker Rene Lalique, was opened in 2011 near the company's factory.

nary_nodes.label: Number of works in museum
evidence: It houses over 650 "exceptional works" including Art Nouveau jewelry, Art Deco glass and contemporary crystal, according to the museum website.

nary_nodes.label: Mayor's anger over burglary
evidence: The mayor of Wingen-sur-Moder, a town of 1,500 inhabitants about 37 miles northwest of Strasbourg, told local newspaper Les Dernieres nouvelles d'Alsace (DNA) he was angry about the burglary.

nary_nodes.label: Mayor's claim of security failure
evidence: All the alarms went off, just as they should. And then with the security company, apparently, there was a major failure on their part: they didn't intervene right away, they didn't inform the gendarmes.

nary_nodes.label: Mayor's claim of specialist thieves
evidence: They were surely well informed to carry out this job in that way; they must be... specialists.

nary_nodes.label: Louvre museum heist
evidence: Thieves made off with $102 million worth of jewelry, including some of the old French crown jewels, from the Louvre in a raid lasting less than eight minutes.

nary_nodes.label: Value of Louvre heist
evidence: Thieves made off with $102 million worth of jewelry
Thieves made off with $102 million worth of jewelry, including some of the old French crown jewels, from the Louvre in a raid lasting less than eight minutes.

nary_nodes.label: Arrests in Louvre heist
evidence: The suspected thieves have been arrested and charged, but none of the jewels have been recovered except for a crown that was dropped as the group escaped.

nary_nodes.label: Security audit of Denon Wing
evidence: A security audit found that 35% of the rooms in the Denon Wing, where the stolen jewels were displayed, were not monitored by security cameras, according to Radio France.

nary_nodes.label: Gems not privately insured
evidence: The gems were also not privately insured, in accordance with French law.

nary_nodes.label: Gold theft at Natural History Museum
evidence: Last October, a woman was arrested and charged over the theft of gold from the Natural History Museum in Paris.

nary_nodes.label: Porcelain heist at Adrien Dubouche Museum
evidence: In September, thieves snatched three porcelain works worth millions of dollars and classed as national treasures in a heist at the Adrien Dubouche National Museum in Limoges in central France.

nary_nodes.label: Cognacq-Jay museum heist
evidence: In November 2024, four men with axes and baseball bats smashed the display cases in broad daylight at the Cognacq-Jay museum in Paris, making off with several 18th-century works.

nary_nodes.label: Insurance payment for Cognacq-Jay heist
evidence: That heist resulted in an insurance payment of over $4 million to the Royal Collection Trust, BBC News reported.

nary_nodes.label: Armed robbery at Saone-et-Loire museum
evidence: The next day, jewelry valued at several million dollars was stolen during an armed robbery at a museum in Saone-et-Loire in central France.
